files.README.md:
# shop-api

REST API generated by [Model2API](https://raulesteveza.github.io/tools/Model2API/) with Ktor. It is a starting point: review it before using it in production.

## Run it

Requires Java 21 and Gradle 9 (or a Gradle wrapper: `gradle wrapper` creates one).

```bash
gradle run
```

Set the variables of `.env.example` in your environment first. The API listens on http://localhost:8080. Its contract is in `openapi.yaml`.

## Test it

```bash
gradle test
```

Each test starts the application anew, so it starts with empty storage.
The tests use a new SQLite file for each test, or the sqlite database in `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (with `TEST_DATABASE_USER` and `TEST_DATABASE_PASSWORD`; its tables are dropped before each test).

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | What it does | Success | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/customers` | List customers | 200 | authenticated |
| `GET` | `/customers/{id}` | Get a customer | 200 | authenticated |
| `POST` | `/customers` | Create a customer | 201 | authenticated |
| `PUT` | `/customers/{id}` | Replace a customer | 200 | authenticated |
| `PATCH` | `/customers/{id}` | Update part of a customer | 200 | authenticated |
| `DELETE` | `/customers/{id}` | Delete a customer | 204 | authenticated |
| `GET` | `/products` | List products | 200 | authenticated |
| `GET` | `/products/{id}` | Get a product | 200 | authenticated |
| `POST` | `/products` | Create a product | 201 | authenticated |
| `PUT` | `/products/{id}` | Replace a product | 200 | authenticated |
| `PATCH` | `/products/{id}` | Update part of a product | 200 | authenticated |
| `DELETE` | `/products/{id}` | Delete a product | 204 | authenticated |
| `GET` | `/orders` | List orders | 200 | authenticated |
| `GET` | `/orders/{id}` | Get an order | 200 | authenticated |
| `POST` | `/orders` | Create an order | 201 | authenticated |
| `PUT` | `/orders/{id}` | Replace an order | 200 | authenticated |
| `PATCH` | `/orders/{id}` | Update part of an order | 200 | authenticated |
| `DELETE` | `/orders/{id}` | Delete an order | 204 | authenticated |

Errors always have the same body: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": [...]}}`. Invalid requests answer 400.

## Storage

Exposed on sqlite. The application creates the tables that are missing when it starts, while you develop; for a real database, use migrations (Model2DB writes them). Embedded objects and lists are stored as JSON text, and references as key columns.

## Authentication

Protected endpoints need a key in the `X-API-Key` header, one of the comma-separated keys in `API_KEYS`. Without `API_KEYS`, every protected request is rejected.

## Structure

```text
src/main/kotlin/com/example/api/
  Application.kt        entry point: wires storage, services and routes
  common/               errors, request bodies, JSON, lists and settings
  model/                domain classes, enums and embedded objects
  dto/                  request bodies and responses
```

package com.example.api

import com.example.api.common.JsonFormat
import com.example.api.common.Settings
import com.example.api.common.installErrors
import com.example.api.database.connectDatabase
import com.example.api.repository.ExposedCustomerRepository
import com.example.api.repository.ExposedOrderRepository
import com.example.api.repository.ExposedProductRepository
import com.example.api.routes.customerRoutes
import com.example.api.routes.orderRoutes
import com.example.api.routes.productRoutes
import com.example.api.security.installSecurity
import com.example.api.service.CustomerService
import com.example.api.service.OrderService
import com.example.api.service.ProductService
import io.ktor.serialization.kotlinx.json.json
import io.ktor.server.application.Application
import io.ktor.server.application.ApplicationStopped
import io.ktor.server.application.install
import io.ktor.server.engine.embeddedServer
import io.ktor.server.netty.Netty
import io.ktor.server.plugins.contentnegotiation.ContentNegotiation
import io.ktor.server.routing.routing

/** Starts the API on PORT (8080 by default) with the settings of the environment. */
fun main() {
    val port = System.getenv("PORT")?.toIntOrNull() ?: 8080
    embeddedServer(Netty, port = port) { module(Settings.fromEnvironment()) }.start(wait = true)
}

/** The API: JSON, errors, authentication, storage and routes. */
fun Application.module(settings: Settings) {
    install(ContentNegotiation) { json(JsonFormat) }
    installErrors()
    installSecurity(settings)

    // Each repository keeps its items in the database with Exposed
    val database = connectDatabase(settings)
    monitor.subscribe(ApplicationStopped) { database.close() }
    val customerRepository = ExposedCustomerRepository(database.database)
    val productRepository = ExposedProductRepository(database.database)
    val orderRepository = ExposedOrderRepository(database.database)
    val customerService = CustomerService(customerRepository)
    val productService = ProductService(productRepository)
    val orderService = OrderService(orderRepository, customerRepository, productRepository)

    routing {
        customerRoutes(customerService)
        productRoutes(productService)
        orderRoutes(orderService)
    }
}

package com.example.api.dto

import com.example.api.common.Checks
import com.example.api.common.JsonKind
import com.example.api.model.Address
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject

/** Body of a request that creates or replaces a customer. */
@Serializable
data class CustomerCreate(
    val name: String? = null,
    val email: String? = null,
    val password: String? = null,
    val phone: String? = null,
    val address: Address? = null,
) {
    companion object {
        /** What the body must meet, checked on its JSON before it is read. */
        fun rules(checks: Checks, json: JsonObject) {
            checks.required(json, "name")
            checks.notNull(json, "name")
            checks.kind(json, "name", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.required(json, "email")
            checks.notNull(json, "email")
            checks.kind(json, "email", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.required(json, "password")
            checks.notNull(json, "password")
            checks.kind(json, "password", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.notNull(json, "phone")
            checks.kind(json, "phone", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.required(json, "address")
            checks.notNull(json, "address")
            checks.kind(json, "address", JsonKind.OBJECT)
            checks.nested(json, "address", Address::rules)
        }
    }
}

data class OrderCreate(
    val customerId: Long? = null,
    val lines: List<OrderLine>? = null,
    val status: OrderStatus? = null,
    val total: Double? = null,
    val notes: String? = null,
) {

        fun rules(checks: Checks, json: JsonObject) {
            checks.required(json, "customerId")

            checks.required(json, "lines")
            checks.notNull(json, "lines")
            checks.kind(json, "lines", JsonKind.LIST)
            checks.each(json, "lines", OrderLine::rules)
            checks.required(json, "status")
            checks.notNull(json, "status")
            checks.kind(json, "status", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.required(json, "total")
            checks.notNull(json, "total")
            checks.kind(json, "total", JsonKind.NUMBER)
            checks.kind(json, "notes", JsonKind.TEXT)
        }
    }

            id = item.id,
            customerId = item.customerId,
            lines = item.lines,
            status = item.status,
            total = item.total,
            notes = item.notes,
            createdAt = item.createdAt,
            updatedAt = item.updatedAt,
